# Behavioural tests: the complete story catalogue

<!-- Generated by pdm run acceptance-stories; edit acceptance/stories.yaml. -->

**944 MCP acceptance cases, 160 test functions, 40 user stories. Every case is assigned to exactly one story.**

Start with a domain task below. Each story gives the user's goal, the starting situation (Given), the action (When), and the expected answer (Then). Its examples explain every test function in plain language; the Cases column counts its parameter variants. Expand the evidence section for every exact test ID and a source link.

An NCIt concept is a coded terminology entry. A caDSR data element defines a data item and its permitted values. Provenance names where an answer came from and its version. Truncation means a limit prevented a complete answer; it is different from no matches.

The [specification and requirement-to-test map](specification.md#4-requirements) remain the authority for behaviour. Stories explain the tests; they do not add requirements. The same shared rule is exercised across different tools and inputs, so a story may cover many cases.

This is an inventory, not a passing test report. [Run reports](../acceptance/README.md#the-report) say what passed, failed or did not run. Fixture cases include recorded responses and contract-crafted scenarios; caDSR credentials are not yet issued. A fixture result does not establish live access, clinical suitability or production search quality. Implementation unit tests and harness self-tests are outside this MCP catalogue.

<a id="discover-tools"></a>

## Discover a dependable set of operations

**User goal:** As an application designer, I want a clear and stable list of supported operations so users are not offered actions the service cannot perform.

**Given:** An application connects using the EVS, caDSR or unified profile selected for the run.

**When:** It asks which tools exist, what their inputs mean and whether they modify data.

**Then:** The list matches the profile, uses the agreed names and arguments, describes supported behaviour only, and stays stable after content calls and during an upstream outage.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The available tool names are exactly those of the selected profile. | 1 | `P-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L124) |
| Tool and schema descriptions contain no unfinished or debugging text. | 1 | `P-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L146) |
| Descriptions and examples do not advertise options that the specification excludes. | 1 | `P-11` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L209) |
| Names follow the common action-led naming convention. | 1 | `P-4` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L224) |
| Retrieving content does not change the advertised tool definitions. | 1 | `P-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L257) |
| A source outage does not make tools disappear or change their definitions. | 1 | `P-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L268) |
| Tools declare that they read external data, do not destroy it, and are safe to repeat. | 1 | `P-10` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L298) |
| Input names and which inputs are mandatory match the specification. | 1 | `P-12` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L309) |

<a id="interpretable-answers"></a>

## Receive answers and errors an application can interpret

**User goal:** As an application designer, I want predictable answer structures so that a domain user sees the correct result or explanation.

**Given:** Each tool declares the structure of its successful answers and errors.

**When:** The application receives a normal answer or provokes an upstream failure.

**Then:** Both responses follow the declared structure, and the declaration admits valid errors while rejecting malformed ones.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Every tool has a valid result schema that accepts the defined errors but rejects an unknown or missing error code. | 1 | `P-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L131) |
| Actual successful results conform to each tool's declared result structure. | 26 | `X-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L138) |
| Actual failure results conform to that structure too. | 26 | `X-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L294) |
| The answer is a named record rather than an unlabelled list or scalar. | 26 | `X-14` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L147) |

<a id="prompts-and-resources"></a>

## Use guided tasks and directly addressable records

**User goal:** As a domain user working through an MCP application, I want task guidance and reusable record addresses that agree with the tools.

**Given:** The profile advertises prompts, fixed resources and parameterized resource addresses.

**When:** The application lists them, asks for a prompt, or reads a record through its address.

**Then:** The offered guidance uses the correct tools in the stated order; records agree with their corresponding tool on identity and release and carry provenance and appropriate reuse hints.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The listed prompts and their required inputs match the profile's specification. | 1 | `P-8` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L335) |
| Prompt instructions are nonempty and name the stated, available tools in the stated order. | 1 | `P-8` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L375) |
| The resource and address-template lists match the profile exactly. | 1 | `P-8` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L398) |
| An address outside the supported resource forms produces an error, not invented content. | 2 | `P-9` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L412) |
| Reading each resource gives the declared data format and agrees with its tool on identity and, where applicable, release. | 7 | `P-9` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L475) |
| Resource content identifies its source and retrieval time, including the unpinned caDSR registry state. | 7 | `P-9` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L500) |
| Each resource carries reuse duration and sharing rules appropriate to its content. | 7 | `P-9` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L522) |
| The index description identifies its concept count, embedding configuration, build time and provenance. | 1 | `P-9` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L537) |

<a id="trace-an-answer"></a>

## Trace an answer back to its source

**User goal:** As a data steward, I want to establish where each answer came from and how related concepts were reached.

**Given:** A call returns content directly or by following terminology relationships.

**When:** I inspect the answer's provenance and the request identifier supplied by my application.

**Then:** Source, retrieval time and method are available, traversal explains its route, upstream attribution fields are preserved, and the request identifier follows the call through the upstream systems and back.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The caller's correlation identifier appears on every upstream request and in the returned provenance. | 1 | `P-7` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L279) |
| Every returned item has the required source, release, retrieval time and delivery information. | 26 | `X-7` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L153) |
| Related items identify depth, relationship, direction and polarity, including genuinely traversed items. | 3 | `X-7` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L164) |
| Codes have their terminology stated separately instead of embedding a prefix or a web address. | 26 | `X-9` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L176) |
| Origin fields supplied by the source are retained unchanged. | 6 | `X-8` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L466) |

<a id="choose-release"></a>

## Choose the terminology release deliberately

**User goal:** As a terminology curator, I want the release I requested so that an unrelated update cannot silently change my evidence.

**Given:** The source may identify both weekly and monthly releases as current, or may no longer serve a requested release.

**When:** I resolve a channel or request content at a particular release.

**Then:** Resolution follows the channel tag, every item names the requested release, and missing, ambiguous or mismatched identity produces an error instead of a substitute answer.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Monthly and weekly each select their own tagged release even when the other appears first. | 2 | `resolve_release-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L40) |
| Two releases claiming the same channel produce an error naming both candidates. | 1 | `resolve_release-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L58) |
| Discovery is marked for immediate refresh rather than reuse as a cached current release. | 1 | `resolve_release-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L71) |
| Each item identifies the release selected for the call. | 15 | `X-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L130) |
| An unserved release returns the specified availability or mismatch error and no substitute content. | 15 | `X-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L268) |
| Content identifying a different release is rejected. | 12 | `X-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L278) |

<a id="keep-session-release"></a>

## Keep terminology consistent within a session

**User goal:** As an analyst, I want related calls to use a consistent implicit NCIt release while retaining the ability to request another release explicitly.

**Given:** A session has selected its first implicit release, and the source's current release can change later.

**When:** I make further calls, including an explicit release override, or the held release is withdrawn.

**Then:** Implicit calls keep the session's release; an explicit override affects only its own call; withdrawal is reported without silently adopting the new release.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| A call omitting the release identifies the resolved NCIt release in its answer. | 15 | `X-22` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L744) |
| The first implicit release survives an explicit override and a source update. | 1 | `X-22` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_release_session.py#L11) |
| Withdrawal of the held release produces an error rather than a fresh implicit selection. | 1 | `X-22` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_release_session.py#L30) |

<a id="reuse-content"></a>

## Reuse stable content without sharing private computed answers

**User goal:** As an application designer, I want reuse instructions that preserve freshness and keep caller-specific computed results private.

**Given:** Discovery lists, pinned terminology content, unpinned registry content and computed matches have different freshness needs.

**When:** The application reads the result's cache duration and sharing scope.

**Then:** Stable lists and pinned content allow public reuse, registry content follows its shorter policy, and computed matching results are private and not reusable from a cache.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Tool, prompt, resource and template lists carry positive reuse durations and public scope. | 4 | `P-5` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_protocol.py#L246) |
| Explicitly pinned content permits positive-duration public reuse. | 15 | `X-13` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L202) |
| Registry content and computed matches receive their distinct required cache policies. | 9 | `X-13` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L246) |

<a id="distinguish-empty-and-failed"></a>

## Distinguish no matches from a service failure

**User goal:** As a domain reviewer, I want to know whether nothing matched or retrieval failed so I do not interpret an outage as absence of relevant data.

**Given:** A source can return an empty answer, refuse a request, return HTML instead of data, or put an error inside an apparently successful response.

**When:** I request content through an affected tool.

**Then:** A valid search with no matches is an empty result with provenance; an unknown record identifier is not_found. Source failures and malformed responses are errors, with a source-declared invalid request distinguished where the contract requires it.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| An unavailable source yields an upstream error or timeout, not empty success. | 26 | `X-5` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L286) |
| Each supported source's success-shaped error response is recognized as failure. | 1 | `X-15` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L429) |
| A valid search with no matches succeeds with an empty result, provenance and no continuation token. | 6 | `X-4` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L450) |
| caDSR requests ask for JSON so that the expected content is retrieved rather than an HTML page. | 1 | `X-15` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L42) |
| An unknown caDSR data element reported inside HTTP success is not_found, never empty success. | 1 | `X-15` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L60) |
| HTML received instead of requested JSON is rejected as an upstream failure. | 1 | `X-15` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L72) |
| A contract-defined caDSR request refusal is presented as an invalid request. | 1 | `X-15` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L86) |

<a id="respect-upstream-capacity"></a>

## Respect source capacity while obtaining an answer

**User goal:** As a service operator, I want calls to avoid redundant retrieval and honour a source's retry delay.

**Given:** A tool may need several upstream reads and a source may ask it to wait before retrying.

**When:** The tool executes a call or receives a rate-limit response.

**Then:** It does not duplicate successful reads within the call and waits for the required delay before retrying the rate-limited endpoint.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Logged upstream requests contain no identical repeated request during the successful call. | 26 | `X-11` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L188) |
| A rate-limited request is retried after the required wait, without an intervening request to that endpoint. | 2 | `X-16` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L399) |

<a id="protect-credentials"></a>

## Use upstream credentials without exposing them

**User goal:** As a service operator, I want authorized upstream access without disclosing credentials to callers or diagnostic output.

**Given:** The fixture service requires a synthetic licence key or caDSR credential.

**When:** A call succeeds or fails using that credential.

**Then:** The credential reaches the intended source but is absent from returned content and, where the harness can inspect them, logs and written files.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The licence key is sent upstream and is absent from answers, logs and files observable to this test transport. | 1 | `X-12` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L321) |
| Error responses do not expose the licence key even when the upstream response includes it. | 1 | `X-12` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L336) |
| The caDSR credential is sent upstream and is absent from answers, logs and files observable to this test transport. | 1 | `X-12` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L356) |

<a id="preserve-attribution"></a>

## Preserve the source's licence attribution

**User goal:** As a content consumer, I want the attribution supplied with an item without invented licence claims.

**Given:** Different source answers may provide licence text, different text, or none.

**When:** I retrieve release-pinned content.

**Then:** Attribution reproduces what that source supplied and adds no licence text of its own.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Supplied licence text is preserved exactly. | 4 | `X-19` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L801) |
| An item carries no additional licence text absent from the source answer. | 4 | `X-19` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L819) |
| Without source-provided licence text, attribution contains no licence text. | 15 | `X-19` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L836) |

<a id="page-and-bound-results"></a>

## Read long results without mistaking a page for the whole answer

**User goal:** As an analyst, I want continuation to preserve my query and version while incomplete answers clearly state their limits.

**Given:** A result contains more items than one page or a caller's bound allows.

**When:** I follow its continuation token or change an argument while attempting to continue.

**Then:** Pages continue without repeats at the same release; incompatible arguments are refused; explicitly stating an already-applied default is allowed; truncation reports its bound and omitted magnitude.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| A deliberately small limit yields explicit truncation information rather than an apparently complete answer. | 4 | `X-10` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L490) |
| Continuation gives the next items without overlap and preserves release identity. | 7 | `X-17` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L536) |
| Changing an applied argument invalidates the continuation token. | 21 | `X-17` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L581) |
| An omitted argument can be stated as its original default on continuation. | 6 | `X-17` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L615) |
| An explicitly supplied default can be omitted on continuation without changing the query. | 6 | `X-17` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L633) |
| Omitting a previously supplied non-default argument is refused. | 5 | `X-17` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L659) |

<a id="preserve-input-intent"></a>

## Preserve the caller's input and reject invalid identifiers

**User goal:** As a domain user, I want my text to reach the source intact and invalid selections to be explained before retrieval.

**Given:** Calls accept bounded numbers, optional defaults, identifiers and free text containing punctuation or query-like characters.

**When:** I submit those inputs across the supported tools.

**Then:** Defaults behave consistently, values below the permitted minimum are refused, malformed identifiers never reach upstream, and valid text remains one unchanged input value.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Omitting an optional argument gives the same answer as supplying its stated default. | 16 | `X-20` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L704) |
| Zero and negative bounded arguments are rejected instead of silently raised to one. | 30 | `X-18` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L735) |
| Invalid identifier variants are refused before any upstream request can carry them. | 312 | `X-23` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L932) |
| A code without a specified local format remains a single encoded upstream path segment. | 1 | `X-23` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L962) |
| Free-text punctuation cannot split, truncate or change the value sent to the source. | 11 | `X-24` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L1041) |

<a id="registry-state"></a>

## Know what registry state an answer represents

**User goal:** As a data steward, I want an honest registry identity and reproducible pins only when caDSR actually publishes them.

**Given:** caDSR may publish no registry release, or a fixture may exercise a future published release contract.

**When:** I resolve the registry state, request pinned content, or continue a registry query.

**Then:** An unpublished state is not assigned an invented release; export metadata remains separate; a published requested release is sent and returned; unavailable releases and incompatible continuations fail.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Unpinned items name the caDSR registry without an invented release identifier or date. | 9 | `X-21` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L220) |
| Asking for an unpublished registry release fails instead of falling back to unpinned content. | 9 | `X-21` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_crosscutting.py#L236) |
| Registry status uses the export's reported date and distribution without claiming a published release. | 1 | `resolve_registry_release-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L116) |
| A fixture-published registry release is returned as published with its identity. | 1 | `resolve_registry_release-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L732) |
| Published-release content requests carry that release and retain its identity and date in provenance. | 1 | `X-21` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L746) |
| A missing release is refused even when the registry publishes other releases. | 1 | `X-21` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L768) |
| A registry continuation token cannot be used with a different release. | 2 | `X-17` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L781) |

<a id="terminology-catalogue"></a>

## Find the terminologies the source actually serves

**User goal:** As a terminology user, I want to discover the available terminologies and their current releases before selecting one.

**Given:** EVS provides a terminology listing.

**When:** I request the available terminologies.

**Then:** The result includes every terminology and current release represented by that source listing.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| No terminology offered by the source is left out of the listing. | 1 | `list_terminologies-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L183) |

<a id="concept-detail"></a>

## Retrieve the concept details needed for a task

**User goal:** As a terminology curator, I want selected concept details with the source's identity and status.

**Given:** A concept has summary information and separately requestable sections.

**When:** I request its identity or one supported detail section.

**Then:** The answer preserves the source's concept identity and status and returns the requested section without unrelated sections; unsupported section selections are refused.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Each supported include choice returns its own section without other optional sections. | 4 | `get_concept-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L94) |
| Descendants cannot be requested as a concept include section. | 1 | `get_concept-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L108) |
| Code, terminology, name and active state are present, with the source's status where supplied. | 2 | `get_concept-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L118) |

<a id="batch-concepts"></a>

## Retrieve several concepts without losing input order or missing codes

**User goal:** As a data steward, I want to align a batch answer with my original code list and see which codes could not be retrieved.

**Given:** The upstream batch endpoint can reorder results and omit unknown codes.

**When:** I request several concepts together.

**Then:** Retrieval uses one batch request, returned concepts follow the requested order, and omitted codes appear explicitly as missing.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| A concept batch is obtained in one upstream request. | 1 | `get_concepts-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L149) |
| A silently omitted upstream code is reported in the missing-code list. | 1 | `get_concepts-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L162) |
| Different requested code orders are retained in the batch answer. | 2 | `get_concepts-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L173) |

<a id="lexical-search"></a>

## Find terminology entries by text or a typed prefix

**User goal:** As a terminology user, I want text search and typeahead to reflect the source's matches without invented rankings.

**Given:** EVS provides ordered text matches, highlights for lexical search, and prefix matches for typeahead.

**When:** I search for text or request suggestions while typing.

**Then:** Source order is retained; lexical pages carry the source's highlights and total; typeahead adds neither highlights nor scores that its source did not supply.

| Prefix suggestions preserve source order and omit unsupported scores and highlights. | 1 | `search_concepts-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L257) |

<a id="indexed-search"></a>

## Search the prepared terminology index with transparent ranking

**User goal:** As an analyst, I want indexed search results tied to the selected terminology release and an explicit error when that index cannot serve my request.

**Given:** A prepared fixture index supports semantic and hybrid search for its own terminology and release.

**When:** I search it and continue through ranked pages.

**Then:** Results carry scores, matched fields and index provenance, the named concept is on the first page, and continuation follows ranking; missing or incompatible indexes are not treated as no matches.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Both index modes return descending scores and index provenance, with the exactly named concept on the first page and a total reflecting the index set. | 2 | `search_concepts-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L460) |
| The continuation token selects the next ranked items. | 2 | `X-17`, `search_concepts-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L491) |
| An index mode unsupported for the selected terminology is an invalid request. | 4 | `search_concepts-4` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L509) |
| A release different from the active index produces a release-mismatch error. | 2 | `search_concepts-5` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L526) |
| A missing index produces a capability-unavailable error rather than empty search results. | 2 | `search_concepts-8` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L575) |

<a id="search-retired"></a>

## Search retired concepts deliberately

**User goal:** As a curator reviewing historical terminology, I want to include retired entries or select them alone without undocumented filtering.

**Given:** The terminology listing defines which statuses count as retired, where it supports that distinction.

**When:** I search normally, request retired-only results, or provide an unsupported retirement option.

**Then:** Retired entries remain in ordinary results, retired-only results contain only retired entries, and invalid options or unusable status definitions are refused across the relevant search modes.

| Typeahead supports the same retired-only selection. | 1 | `search_concepts-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L349) |
| Unsupported retirement values, including an exclusion mode, are refused. | 3 | `search_concepts-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L361) |
| A retired status inconsistent with the terminology's concept-status list is rejected. | 1 | `search_concepts-7` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L371) |
| Retired-only search is refused where the terminology supplies no retired status. | 1 | `search_concepts-7` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L389) |

| Semantic and hybrid modes reject unsupported retirement values too. | 6 | `search_concepts-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L564) |

<a id="hierarchy"></a>

## Explore a concept's hierarchy with clear depth and paging

**User goal:** As a terminology analyst, I want to explore parentage and descendants without assuming a bounded answer is complete.

**Given:** The source supplies a hierarchy and ordered paths from a concept to the root.

**When:** I request paths, a depth above the permitted maximum, or several hierarchy pages.

**Then:** Paths retain source order, depth is capped and reported when it limits the answer, and all pages together preserve the source's ordered concepts without repeats.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|

| Every supplied path to the root is returned in the source's code order. | 1 | `get_concept_hierarchy-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L736) |
| Hierarchy continuation pages reconstruct the source listing without duplicate concepts. | 1 | `get_concept_hierarchy-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L751) |

<a id="neighbourhood"></a>

## Explore different relationship kinds without hiding limits or exclusions

**User goal:** As a domain analyst, I want a balanced view of requested relationships and a clear distinction between positive and exclusion relationships.

**Given:** A concept has several relationship kinds, potentially large inverse lists, and coded negative relationships.

**When:** I explore its neighbourhood with global or per-kind bounds and optional negative traversal.

**Then:** One kind does not consume another's allowance, truncation identifies affected kinds, negative polarity follows relationship codes, and excluded links are followed only when requested.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |

| A supplied per-kind allowance limits the nodes that kind contributes and records its truncation. | 2 | `get_concept_neighborhood-6` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L802) |
| A failed call's reported attempts agree with actual requests, including retries; this case does not prove every internal request-budget boundary. | 2 | `get_concept_neighborhood-5` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L846) |
| Renaming a relationship cannot change its negative or positive classification. | 1 | `get_concept_neighborhood-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L874) |
| Negative edges remain visible and marked, but traversal beyond them requires explicit inclusion. | 2 | `get_concept_neighborhood-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L919) |
| An excessive node limit is capped and the result reports the applied maximum. | 1 | `get_concept_neighborhood-4` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_evs.py#L947) |

<a id="data-element"></a>

## Retrieve a data element without guessing its identity or version

**User goal:** As a data steward, I want to reuse a data element's definition and optional sections while resolving familiar question text unambiguously.

**Given:** The registry has versioned data elements and question text that may identify one, several or no records.

**When:** I request a data element by identity or question, and select optional details.

**Then:** The record preserves its own fields, version and statuses; requested details are included; ambiguity identifies candidates; absence and an unsupported lookup route are distinguished.

| The fixture question Date of birth produces an ambiguity error naming candidate public identifiers. | 1 | `get_data_element-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L262) |
| Unsupported lookup by long name reports capability unavailable. | 1 | `get_data_element-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L280) |
| Question text with no matching data element reports not found. | 1 | `get_data_element-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L525) |

<a id="matching-candidates"></a>

| A candidate without a source concept omits that optional concept instead of inventing one or inserting a null value. | 1 | `match_value_meanings-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_cadsr.py#L689) |

## Ground a clinical concept across terminology and metadata

**User goal:** As a domain analyst, I want to trace Ewing Sarcoma from its NCIt concept into data-element uses, permissible values and optional commons values.

**Given:** The fixtures provide concept C4817 and its uses, with separate scenarios for a changed release, unusual search order and a bounded retrieval step.

**When:** I ground the concept or text, optionally naming a commons.

**Then:** Each step returns its source content under the appropriate content states; text follows the search's first result; release conflicts fail; and a bounded step does not discard independently retrieved steps.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The answer and registry-dependent items distinguish the selected NCIt release from the unpinned caDSR registry. | 1 | `ground_value-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L47) |
| A different release on either the terminology or graph surface produces a release mismatch. | 2 | `ground_value-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L67) |
| Concept, data-element uses and permissible values match their sources; without a commons request there is no stored-value section. | 1 | `ground_value-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L80) |
| Adding GDC returns the literal stored values and fields from its mapping source. | 1 | `ground_value-2` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L100) |
| Text grounding uses the first search result even when another concept's name looks closer. | 1 | `ground_value-3` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L116) |
| A capped data-element step reports its own truncation while the independent permissible-value step remains complete. | 1 | `ground_value-4` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L134) |

<a id="expand-cohort"></a>

## Build a cohort code set with explicit exclusions

**User goal:** As a researcher defining a terminology code set, I want descendants and exclusions to be visible and deliberate; this operation does not select patients.

**Given:** A fixture root has descendants and exclusion relationships to some of them.

**When:** I expand the cohort with default exclusions, explicitly include negative relationships, or set a small node limit.

**Then:** Membership follows the bounded hierarchy and the root's exclusions; exclusions remain explained even when included; the node limit counts the root too.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Default membership removes the root's excluded codes; explicit negative inclusion retains them while both modes list the exclusion assertions. | 2 | `expand_cohort-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L187) |
| A small node limit includes the root in its count and reports the truncated result size. | 1 | `expand_cohort-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L216) |

<a id="harmonize-dictionary"></a>

## Harmonize a dictionary while keeping unmatched columns visible

**User goal:** As a data steward, I want matching candidates and sample-value alignments for dictionary columns without losing fields the source cannot match.

**Given:** The fixture dictionary contains Patient Gender and Freezer Shelf Label, with matches only for the first, and sample values with value-meaning matches.

**When:** I harmonize the dictionary with its descriptions and sample values.

**Then:** Each column is matched once using its description, unmatched columns remain explicitly listed, and value alignments are those supplied by the matching service under the same registry state.

| Behaviour checked | Cases | Requirements | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Each column is submitted once with its description; Freezer Shelf Label remains unmatched and candidate records retain the registry state. | 1 | `harmonize_data_dictionary-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L255) |
| Patient Gender's sample-value alignments match the source's value-meaning and concept answers. | 1 | `harmonize_data_dictionary-1` | [Test](../acceptance/tests/test_workflow.py#L275) |
